separate.title: Claude Code docs: Best practices for Claude Code
separate.quote: Separate research and planning from implementation to avoid solving the wrong problem.

wrong-problem.title: Claude Code docs: Best practices for Claude Code
wrong-problem.quote: Letting Claude jump straight to coding can produce code that solves the wrong problem.

phases.title: Claude Code docs: Best practices for Claude Code
phases.quote: The recommended workflow has four phases:

plan-mode.title: Claude Code docs: Choose a permission mode
plan-mode.quote: Plan mode tells Claude to research and propose changes without making them. Claude reads files, runs shell commands to explore, and writes a plan, but does not edit your source.

enter-plan.title: Claude Code docs: Choose a permission mode
enter-plan.quote: Enter plan mode by pressing Shift+Tab or prefixing a single prompt with /plan.

start-plan.title: Claude Code docs: Best practices for Claude Code
start-plan.quote: Enter plan mode by pressing Shift+Tab until the status bar shows ⏸ plan mode on, or start the session with claude --permission-mode plan. Claude reads files and answers questions without making changes.

approve-manual.title: Claude Code docs: Choose a permission mode
approve-manual.quote: Yes, manually approve edits: approve and review each edit individually.

keep-planning.title: Claude Code docs: Choose a permission mode
keep-planning.quote: No, keep planning: stay in plan mode and tell Claude what to change.

ctrl-g.title: Claude Code docs: Choose a permission mode
ctrl-g.quote: Press Ctrl+G to open the proposed plan in your default text editor and edit it directly before Claude proceeds.

approve-exits.title: Claude Code docs: Choose a permission mode
approve-exits.quote: Approving a plan exits plan mode and switches the session to the permission mode each approve option describes, so Claude starts editing.

overhead.title: Claude Code docs: Best practices for Claude Code
overhead.quote: Plan mode is useful, but also adds overhead.

one-sentence.title: Claude Code docs: Best practices for Claude Code
one-sentence.quote: If you could describe the diff in one sentence, skip the plan.

planning-useful.title: Claude Code docs: Best practices for Claude Code
planning-useful.quote: Planning is most useful when you’re uncertain about the approach, when the change modifies multiple files, or when you’re unfamiliar with the code being modified.

check.title: Claude Code docs: Best practices for Claude Code
check.quote: Give Claude a check it can run: tests, a build, a screenshot to compare.

failing-test.title: Claude Code docs: Best practices for Claude Code
failing-test.quote: write a failing test that reproduces the issue, then fix it

commit-step.title: Claude Code docs: Best practices for Claude Code
commit-step.quote: Ask Claude to commit with a descriptive message and create a PR.

course-correct.title: Claude Code docs: Best practices for Claude Code
course-correct.quote: Correct Claude as soon as you notice it going off track.

git-commit.title: Git documentation: git-commit
git-commit.quote: Create a new commit containing the current contents of the index and the given log message describing the changes.

approve-auto.title: Claude Code docs: Choose a permission mode
approve-auto.quote: Yes, and use auto mode: approve and start in auto mode.
